 Here are the Cricket Predictions for the Women's Big Bash League 2026 - 10th Match - Adelaide Strikers Women vs Brisbane Heat Women and 11th Match - Sydney Thunder Women vs Perth Scorchers Women, to be played on the 5th of November at the Drummoyne Oval, Sydney.
 Match Prediction - Adelaide Strikers Women v Brisbane Heat Women 
 10th Match - Adelaide Strikers Women vs Brisbane Heat Women (Drummoyne Oval, Sydney) 
 Ground Stat:
 Average 1st Innings Total at Drummoyne Oval, Sydney (Women's Big Bash League) - 128 
 Average 2nd Innings Total at Drummoyne Oval, Sydney (Women's Big Bash League) - 119 
 Current Form Adelaide Strikers Women:
 Adelaide Strikers Women are currently placed at the 4th position on points table with 1 win to their credit. They have 2 points to their name. Their NRR is 1.050. 
 The top run scorer for Adelaide Strikers Women in the Women's Big Bash League 2026 is Laura Wolvaardt with 70 runs to her name. 
 The top wicket taker for Adelaide Strikers Women in the Women's Big Bash League 2026 is Amanda Wellington with 3 scalps under her belt. 
 Adelaide Strikers Women have won their previous match against Melbourne Stars Women by 21 runs.
 Adelaide Strikers Women batted first and they posted a huge total of 185 for 2 in 20 overs. Laura Wolvaardt was the star of the show. She smashed 70 runs in only 50 balls, collecting 9 fours. Maia Bouchier and Tahlia McGrath also contributed quite well. Bouchier made 30 while Tahlia McGrath scored 43 runs. A real boost was provided by Madeline Penna in the middle order. She smashed 36 runs in only 13 balls as Adelaide Strikers Women managed to get to a tall total of 185 in 20 overs of play.
 During the chase, Rhys McKenna and Meg Lanning got their team off to a stable but very slow start. Rhys McKenna made 40 off 31 deliveries while Lanning scored 32 off 24 balls. They didn't score at a rapid pace and it didn't help their team much. Annabel Sutherland fought hard and scored 29 quick runs but she also threw it away at a wrong time. The lower order batters failed to infuse any momentum into the innings and Melbourne Stars Women were eventually restricted to 164 for 7 in 20 overs, losing the match by 21 runs.
 Current Form Brisbane Heat Women:
 Brisbane Heat Women are currently placed at the 6th position on points table with 2 losses to their credit. They have 0 point to their name. Their NRR is -0.891. 
 The top run scorer for Brisbane Heat Women in the Women's Big Bash League 2026 is Georgia Redmayne with 58 runs to her name. 
 The top wicket taker for Brisbane Heat Women in the Women's Big Bash League 2026 is Sianna Ginger with 2 scalps under her belt. 
 Brisbane Heat Women have lost their previous match against Sydney Thunder Women by 6 wickets.
 Brisbane Heat Women batted first and they posted a total of 178 for 5 in 20 overs. Charli Knott made 16 runs before being dismissed by Samantha Bates. After her dismissal, Grace Harris and Georgia Redmayne played really well and scored 58 and 57 runs respectively. They laid the foundation for a big total. Orla Prendergast also contributed well with an innings of 28 runs as Brisbane Heat Women managed to get to 178 in 20 overs of play.
 During the chase, Sydney Thunder Women lost the key wicket of Georgia Voll quite early. After her dismissal, Phoebe Litchfield and Anika Learoyd played really well, scoring 41 and 37 runs respectively. After these two got out, it was Heather Knight, who took the responsibility of taking Sydney Thunder Women over the line. She scored 54 runs in 29 balls, stayed not out and steered Sydney Thunder Women to victory in the 17th over itself with 6 wickets in hand.

 Perth Scorchers Women have won their previous match against Melbourne Stars Women by 15 runs.
 Perth Scorchers Women batted first and they posted a total of 124 for 9 in 20 overs. Katie Mack, Beth Mooney and Sophie Devine all played patiently, got the starts but threw it away when they needed to steer the innings forward. The middle order including Freya Kemp and Chloe Piparo also failed terribly. Perth Scorchers Women kept losing wickets in regular succession and they were eventually restricted to an under par total of 124 in 20 overs of play. For Melbourne Stars Women, Sophie Day and Maisy Gibson bowled beautifully and picked up 2 wickets each.
 During the chase, Melbourne Stars Women lost the key wicket of Rhys McKenna quite early. After her dismissal, Meg Lanning took the responsibility of taking Stars Women over the line. She batted with utmost clarity and scored 41 runs in 36 deliveries. Once she was dismissed in the 14th over, Melbourne Stars Women lost their way. They couldn't really face Alana King and Sophie Devine with a controlled approach. King picked up 3 wickets while Devine accounted for 4 scalps as Melbourne Stars Women got bowled out for 109, losing the match by 15 runs.
